core.title: Declare each flow router's entrypoint shape: exposed flag plus actions or reason
core.given: A plan contains a flow router.
core.when: The plan is validated in CONFIRM. Every flow router in the plan is checked, including unchanged ones.
core.then: Every flow router declares whether it is runtime-exposed. exposed:true must list at least one journey router action name expected to reach it. exposed:false must give a reason.
prefer: Set exposed explicitly on every flow router.
List actions by their journey router action names, meaning the actions expected to reach the flow router.
avoid: exposed:true with an empty or missing actions list.
exposed:false with no reason, or with an empty or placeholder reason that only fills the field.
Putting user/system flow IDs in actions instead of journey router action names.
Treating a passing result from this check as proof of runtime reachability. The planner validates shape only.
core.why: Each flow router must state whether it is runtime-exposed and which journey router actions are expected to reach it. That keeps its entrypoint shape explicit and checkable.
evidence: The confirm-phase shape check over every flow router declaration in the plan passes.
Every flow router has exposed set. Each exposed:true flow router has actions length >= 1, given as journey router action names. Each exposed:false flow router has a reason.
On failure, the report names flow_router_id, exposed, actions, reason and field_path.
verification: Presence-only schema check over every flow router declaration in the plan: exposed:true requires actions length >= 1; exposed:false requires a reason; actions must be journey router action names, not user/system flow IDs.
Reason is checked for presence only; no reason-content quality check is part of this check, so verifiers must not add subjective reason validation.
Runs only in the CONFIRM phase and is confirm-blocking.
Severity: 3. Disposition: strict; findings are blocking, not warnings.
Scope limit: the check validates declaration shape only; it does not verify that the listed journey router actions actually reach the flow router at runtime.
On failure, the report names the flow router id, its exposed value, its actions, its reason, and the path to the offending field.

Realization needs an observer that enumerates every flow router declaration in the plan, covering unchanged declarations as well as new or edited ones, and a phase observer that reports when CONFIRM is active.

fires: CONFIRM evaluates a plan that contains any flow router declaration, whether or not the current change touched it.
In CONFIRM, a flow router has no exposed value.
In CONFIRM, a flow router declares exposed:true with an empty or missing actions list.
In CONFIRM, a flow router declares exposed:false without a reason.
In CONFIRM, a flow router's actions list contains user/system flow IDs instead of journey router action names.
doesNotFire: Checking whether the listed journey router actions actually reach the flow router at runtime. This check validates shape only.
Any phase other than CONFIRM. This check runs only in CONFIRM.

neutralityNotes: This convention is a plan-content schema rule over a product-domain artifact (user/system flow plans and their flow router declarations), so nearly everything survives into the core unchanged; journey router, flow router and user/system flow are domain vocabulary, not stack specifics. The only stack-specific residue is the validator/template/variant ids, marked bunOnly, with the check described generically in core.verification. Per-rule severity (3) and disposition (strict) are rule metadata and stay in core.verification, not in the profile and not bunOnly. The phase value CONFIRM is treated as shared ATDD process vocabulary rather than stack machinery; a stack realizing a different phase model would bind it through its own phase observer (both facts are needs_new_observer). No profile keys are required: the core binds to no stack structure (no path, suffix, tool or idiom) - where plan artifacts live and how flow router declarations are enumerated is realization detail deferred to the required observer described in core.verification, and no vocabulary key fits (nor is one missing) for that observer.
